deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. This page belongs to Gauss's 1818 work on the latitude of the new Göttingen observatory. The previous page reduces circle readings of Polaris (upper and lower culmination) and Arcturus to values of the form 51°31'49" ± δ, with δ = +1.99". Here Gauss reduces two stars from mean to apparent place.

A. gamma ANDROMEDAE, LOWER CULMINATION, 1818 MAY 12.
(1) Mean place 1818.0: α0 = 28°11'29.37" (= 1h52m45.96s) and δ0 = +41°27'3.79".
- Precession (plus proper motion) from Jan 0 to May 12 is +19.69" in α and +6.41" in δ.
- To Jun 11 it is +24.15" and +7.86".
- These match annual rates of about 54.7"/yr and 17.8"/yr.
- Mean place of date: α = 28°11'49.06", δ = 41°27'10.20".
- The '0d44' is the fraction of a day: the lower culmination (sidereal time about 13h52m) falls about 0.44 d after noon. [interpretation mine]
(2) Auxiliary angles for May 12.
- Sun's longitude ☉ = 51°30'. Adding 2°23' gives θ = 53°53'. This satisfies tan θ = tan ☉ / cos ε (my check: 53°53.1').
- Mean lunar node Ω = 38°9'. Subtracting 7°50' gives φ = 30°19'.
- 28°12' is the star's α rounded.
(3) Aberration, written in amplitude-phase form [notation mine]:
- Δα cos δ = -κ(cos α cos ☉ cos ε + sin α sin ☉) = -κM cos(α-θ).
- Here M cos θ = cos ☉ cos ε and M sin θ = sin ☉.
- Gauss's logarithmic products:
  - log(κM) = 1.3003n, log cos(α-θ) = 9.9548 (α-θ = -25°41'), log sec δ = 0.1252. Sum 1.3803n, so Δα = -24.00".
  - Declination part: 1.3003n + log sin(θ-α) 9.6369 + log sin δ 9.8208 = 0.7580n, giving -5.73".
  - The remaining aberration term in δ, -κ cos ☉ sin ε cos δ, is presumably the -4.03".
(4) Nutation, same device. Write Δψ = -P sin Ω and Δε = Q cos Ω, with N cos φ = Q cos Ω and N sin φ = P sin ε sin Ω. Then:
- Δα = -P cos ε sin Ω - N cos(α-φ) tan δ.
- Δδ = -N sin(φ-α).
- Gauss's log N = 0.9439, so N = 8.79".
- First RA term: -10.22".
- Second RA term: 0.9439n + log cos(α-φ) 9.9997 + log tan δ 9.9460 = 0.8896n, giving -7.76".
- δ term: 0.9439n + log sin(α-φ) 8.5674 = 9.5113n, giving -0.32".
- Solving back gives Q ≈ 9.65" and P ≈ 18.04". Note P/Q ≈ 2 cot 2ε.
(5) Small terms, presumably solar nutation and similar: -0.99 and -0.18 in α; +0.21 and -0.41 in δ. I cannot identify these individually.
(6) Totals:
- α: 49.06 - 24.00 - 10.22 - 7.76 - 0.99 - 0.18 = 5.91, so α_app = 28°11'5.91" = 1h52m44.39s.
- δ: 10.20 - 5.73 + 0.21 - 4.03 - 0.32 - 0.41 = -0.08, so δ_app = 41°26'59.92".

B. ARCTURUS, APPARENT DECLINATION EVERY 10 DAYS (continued from the previous page and onto the next).
- Logarithm of the refraction at Arcturus's meridian zenith distance (z ≈ 31.4°): 1.54531, i.e. 35.1".
- Model: Δδ = p(t) + A sin(☉+298°25') + B sin(Ω+320°9') + C sin(2☉+326°).
  - p(t) is precession plus proper motion from 1818.0: -0.52" per 10 days, i.e. -19.0"/yr.
  - log A = 1.0949, so A = 12.44". This is the declination aberration amplitude for κ = 20.25 (verified, including the phase 298°25').
  - log B = 0.9002, so B = 7.95". This is the nutation amplitude for P ≈ 18.04, Q ≈ 9.65 (phase 320°9' verified).
  - log C = 9.664 - 10, so C = 0.461". This is the solar (semiannual) nutation term.
- Arguments tabulated:
  - ☉ = 99°14', 108°45', 118°16', 127°48' for Jul 1-31.
  - Ω = 35°31', 34°59', 34°27', 33°55' (regressing 32' per 10 days).
  - 2☉ = 198°28', 217°30', 236°32', 255°36'.
  - Nov 3: ☉ = 221°27', Ω = 28°50', 2☉ = 82°54'.
- Rows give log sin of each argument. Example, Jul 1: 9.7859, 8.8783n, 9.428. Adding the amplitude logs gives +7.60, -0.60, +0.12.
- The last column is the total correction to the mean declination 20°8'5.57" (1818.0, previous page): -2.37, -1.59, -1.06, -0.79, -0.80, -1.11, -1.69, -2.60, -12.91.
- The values for Jun 1, 11 and 21 (-5.92, -4.56, -3.27) are carried over from the previous page. There they produced apparent δ = 20°7'59.66", 61.01", 62.30".

PURPOSE. Apparent places are needed to turn meridian-circle zenith distances into the latitude (φ = δ + z for Arcturus) and to check the instrument and clock. The result is about 51°31'48", consistent with Gauss's adopted 51°31'47.85".
errors: Jun 21 (carried from the previous page): -8.97 + 5.87 - 0.53 + 0.26 = -3.37, not -3.27. The individual terms check: the nutation term is -7.95·sin(356°11') = -0.53 and the solar term is +0.26. So the apparent declination should be 62.20", not 62.30". This is a 0.1" arithmetic slip, copied onto this page.
Jun 1: the sum of the previous page's terms is -5.91 (consistent with 59.66"), but -5.92 is written here. This is a 0.01" rounding inconsistency.

gamma And aberration: with κ = 20.25" (the value implied by the Arcturus amplitude) and ☉ = 51°30', I get κM = 19.62 (log 1.2927), giving Δα = -23.59" and Δδ term -5.63". Gauss's log 1.3003 (19.97) gives -24.00" and -5.73". Likewise κ cos☉ sinε cosδ = 3.76" against his -4.03". Possibly other small terms are absorbed, or a slightly different argument was used. Unresolved; a possible ~0.3-0.4" discrepancy.

The written factor '9.9797' (if read correctly) must be 9.9997 = log cos 2°7'. Only 9.9997 reproduces Gauss's own result 0.8896n (7.76"). Either the transcription is wrong or Gauss slipped in writing but computed correctly.

results.what: Reduction of mean to apparent place (precession, annual aberration, lunar and solar nutation) using amplitude-phase (single-sine) forms with logarithms; precomputed star constants for Arcturus (12.44", 298°25'; 7.95", 320°9'; 0.461", 326°)
results.modern_name: Apparent-place reduction with star constants (precursor of Besselian/independent day numbers)
results.usually_credited_to: Bradley/Lalande/Delambre for the formulas; Bessel (Tabulae Regiomontanae 1830) for the systematic day-number scheme

results.what: Nutation constants implied: obliquity ≈ 9.65", longitude ≈ 18.04" (ratio 2cot2ε); aberration 20.25"
results.modern_name: Constants of nutation and aberration (early-19th-century values)
results.usually_credited_to: Bradley (discovery); values of the Maskelyne/Laplace/Delambre era

results.what: Latitude determination of the Göttingen observatory from Polaris, Arcturus and gamma And with the meridian circle (1818)

deep.surprise_reason: This is entirely routine observatory reduction work, done carefully. Its only interest is documentary: it shows which aberration and nutation constants Gauss used in 1818 (κ = 20.25", nutation ≈ 9.65"/18.04") and a small arithmetic slip.

checkable.asserts: The aberration amplitude in declination for Arcturus (α≈211.8°, δ≈20.135°, ε≈23.464°) with κ=20.25 is ≈12.44" (log 1.0949)
The phase of the Arcturus aberration term is ≈298.4° (Gauss 298°25')
The Arcturus nutation amplitude with P=18.04, Q=9.65 is ≈7.95" (log 0.9002)
The Jul 1 aberration term for Arcturus is ≈ +7.60"
The Jun 21 total is -3.37, not -3.27 as written
The gamma And corrections sum to 5.91" (RA) and -0.08" (Dec, giving 41°26'59.92")
The nutation RA term is ≈7.76", requiring the factor log cos = 9.9997
The 'Const Refr' 1.54531 is ≈35.1", the mean refraction at Arcturus's meridian zenith distance at Göttingen

transcription_corrections: '0°44' is more likely 0d44 (fraction of a day of the lower culmination after noon).
In the nutation column, '9.9797' should be 9.9997 (log cos 2°7'); only this reproduces 0.8896n.
Column headers 298.25, 320.9, 326 are phase constants 298°25', 320°9', 326°; the column entries are ☉, Ω, 2☉ in degrees and minutes (e.g. 99°14', 35°31', 198°28').
